key_insight: An agentic LLM system using ReAct-style tool use can accurately answer natural-language questions and run statistical analyses on TCGA clinical data with auditable traces.
clinical_relevance: It could make large cancer clinical repositories easier to query for research by returning clinically contextualized answers, survival analyses, and verified outputs.
method: LLM acts as a ReAct agent that selects among eight tools
Performs data extraction, descriptive statistics, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, log-rank tests, and hypothesis testing
Verifies results against the curated TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource and provides source attribution
evidence_signal: On TCGA-Agent-Bench, the system achieved 93.4% overall accuracy across 440 queries, outperforming rule-based, single-pass LLM, and RAG baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on tool design and data coverage, so a CDR-only setup can miss important fields like drug treatments, TNM components, and biomarkers.
paper_title: A ReAct Agentic AI System for Natural Language Querying and Statistical Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas Clinical Data
